newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebels say resume advance on Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels say resume advance on Kinshasa.

text.p: Zaire rebels said on Sunday they had abandoned a pledge to South African President Nelson Mandela and resumed their advance towards the capital.

Rebel "foreign minister" Bizima Karaha also told a news conference in Lubumbashi that the rebels would abandon a South African peace initiative and storm Kinshasa if Archbishop Laurent Monsengwo accepts his election as speaker of the Zaire parliament.

Karaha said that over the past few days Zairean troops backed by the Angolan rebel group UNITA and former Rwandan troops had attacked rebel positions near the town of Kenge, 200 km (125 miles) east of Kinshasa, but had been driven back.

"Mobutu (Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko) is a devil and a trickster and has used the talks to reinforce his troops, bring in UNITA elements, former Rwandan troops and consolidate his position in Kinshasa," he said.
"Our response to this is that we are abandoning our pledge and we are now advancing and will continue to advance. We shall now talk and fight, and fight and talk."
Karaha said rebel forces were very near Kinshasa but declined to give details. He said they had captured some UNITA troops. "I will parade them here in Lubumbashi in the next few days," he added.
The official said that Monsengwo and unnamed foreign countries were trying to stop a revolution in Zaire.
"If he (Monsengwo) accepts the job then we will abandon talks and Monsengwo will bear the consequences of what will happen in Kinshasa," Karaha said.
"Monsengwo has got responsibilities and he must not repeat what he did a few years ago. He is the one who stopped the revolution," he added.
Monsengwo, archbishop of the northeastern city of Kisangani, was elected on Saturday as part of preparations for Mobutu to hand over power to some transitional authority.
The post of speaker has been vacant since a combined move by Mobutu's followers and the radical UDPS opposition ousted Monsengwo two years ago.

Karaha, who said he was speaking on behalf of rebel leader Laurent Kabila, said the transfer of power in Zaire "shall only be from Mobutu Sese Seko to Mr Kabila". "Nothing else will be acceptable to us," he added.
"We are not going to negotiate with anybody else other than Mobutu. We shall not even deal with Monsengwo, who is just another confusionist in Zaire's politics," said Karaha.
